name: gather-research
description: Turn a business question into a customer research report. Gather researches the company, designs an interview guide, runs simulated interviews with the target audience, and returns a branded report link with findings and quotes.

interface.longDescription:
Gather turns a business question into a customer research report.

Tell ChatGPT the company and the decision you are weighing, like which of two messages to lead with, why buyers pick a competitor, or how a price change will land. Name the options and Gather tests them word for word. Gather researches the company, designs an interview guide, runs simulated interviews with your target audience on Gather's research platform, and writes a branded report: an answer to your question, key findings, themes, quotes, and how the audience chose between options.

You get a report link right away. It shows live progress, then the finished report. Reports with 10 interviews take about 10 minutes, and 30 interviews (the default) take about 16 minutes. Gather also emails the report to you when it is ready.

Who it is for: marketers, product managers, founders and researchers who want a fast, directional read on a target audience before a launch or a campaign.

With your own Gather workspace you can also get answers and quotes from your studies, ask your buyer personas, design a study with real people for your approval, create content from completed studies, and export responses. Each of these is its own tool. Launching a study to real people needs Gather credits.

Limitations: results from reports come from simulated interviews and are directional. They are not a survey of real people. You sign in with a work email and use a Gather workspace; you can create one for your company as you connect, named after your email domain. The number of reports a workspace can start each month depends on its Gather account, and so does launching studies to real people.
capabilities: Answer questions from your Gather research
defaultPrompt: Use Gather to test which message makes small-team leads switch from Confluence to Notion.
Run a 10-interview Gather report on how freelance designers would react to a Canva Pro price increase.
Ask Gather why new parents would or would not pay for a baby sleep coaching app.

positive.description: Start a messaging report for a named company and question.
positive.prompt: Use Gather to run a 10-interview report for Notion (notion.so): which message makes team leads at small software companies switch from Confluence?
positive.expected_behavior: Starts one report and returns its id (rpt_...) and a report link right away. The link shows live progress, then the finished report. The reply says the report takes about 10 minutes.

positive.prompt: Use Gather to compare two headlines for Notion with 10 interviews: "Write, plan, share" or "Your wiki, docs and projects together". Which makes team leads more likely to try it?
positive.expected_behavior: Starts one report with exactly those two headlines as the options and returns its id and report link right away. When completed, the option choice shows the two headlines word for word plus "None of these".

positive.description: Check a running report, then get its results when it completes.
positive.expected_behavior: While running: the status, the current stage and the report link. When completed (about 10 minutes for 10 interviews): the headline, the answer, key findings, the option choice, themes, quotes from simulated respondents and the report link.

positive.description: List reports started with this connection.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists reports newest first, each with its status, company, question and report link. The test account already has a completed report.

positive.description: Pricing question with a named audience.
positive.prompt: Use Gather to test how US freelance designers would react to Canva raising Pro to $20 a month. Run 10 interviews.
positive.expected_behavior: Starts a report for that audience and returns the report link right away. When completed, the findings explain how the simulated designers reacted to the price change and why.

positive.prompt: Ask Gather whether new parents would pay $15 a month for a baby sleep coaching app called Lullo. Use 10 consumer interviews.
positive.expected_behavior: Starts a consumer (b2c) report and returns the report link right away. When completed, the findings and quotes cover whether and why the simulated parents would pay.

positive.description: Ask about the workspace's own research.
positive.prompt: Ask Gather what our buyers say about pricing.
positive.expected_behavior: Answers from the test workspace's completed studies and added files, with counted numbers and word-for-word quotes, and shares the answer as written. It does not start a report. If the research does not cover pricing, it says so.

positive.prompt: What Gather studies do we have, and which are still running?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the test workspace's studies with each one's status (draft, live, in review or completed) and study id.

positive.description: Ask one of the workspace's buyer personas.
positive.prompt: Ask one of our Gather buyer personas what would make them switch vendors.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the personas, asks one of them, and shares its answer, saying the answer is simulated rather than a quote from a real person. If the persona's research does not cover the question, it says so.

positive.description: Design a study with real people, without launching it.
positive.prompt: Use Gather to design a study with 20 IT leaders on why they switch identity providers.
positive.expected_behavior: Relays Gather's questions about anything missing (objective, audience, who qualifies) one at a time, continuing the same design by its study_id, then shares a research plan and interview guide link for approval. The interview is built only when the user approves. Nothing is launched to real people.

negative.description: Asks Gather to email a survey to the user's customers now. With the test account, Gather never launches a study to real people: reports use simulated interviews, gather_design_study only designs a study for the user's approval, and gather_launch_study refuses for the test account. ChatGPT should not claim a survey was sent, and may offer a simulated report or a study design instead.
negative.prompt: Use Gather to email a survey to our 500 customers right now.

negative.description: Asks to delete reports. Gather has no tool that deletes anything, so ChatGPT should say it cannot delete reports and call no tool.
A request unrelated to customer research. ChatGPT should not call any Gather tool.
negative.prompt: What will the weather be in Paris tomorrow?

review.commerce_description: Gather does not sell products or take payments in ChatGPT.

publication.release_notes: Each workspace action is now its own tool, with its own description, inputs and read or write hints: gather_research_answer, gather_find_quotes, gather_list_studies, gather_list_personas, gather_ask_persona, gather_research_ideas, gather_list_content, gather_create_content, gather_design_study, gather_set_study_audience, gather_get_test_link, gather_launch_study, gather_export_responses, gather_run_simulation and gather_get_simulation. They replace gather_ask.
